label: prf:staircase-corner-hook
title: Proof of staircase corner hook
html:
Proof. Proof of staircase corner hook

Proof. The corner cell (0, 0) has arm length k - 1 (the row 0 of \rho_k has k cells, so k - 1 cells lie strictly to the right of the corner) and leg length k - 1 (the column 0 has k cells, so k - 1 cells lie strictly below the corner). Adding the corner cell itself gives h_{\mathrm{corner}}(\rho_k) = (k-1) + (k-1) + 1 = 2k - 1. \square

This combinatorial identity makes the exponent of the staircase EW-residual conjecture available: the observed pairwise eigenvalue ratio q^{1/h_{\mathrm{corner}}(\rho_k)} in the spectrum of \beta_{\mathrm{EW}} \, \bowtie_K^{\mathrm{minimal}} on V_{\rho_k} matches this corner hook as the inverse exponent. For k = 3 that is the q^{1/5} factor which takes the cot \theta_W gap from 2.19\% to 0.13\%; for k = 4 it is the q^{1/7} scale reported at relative error 0.14\% in the dim-768 spectrum.

Availability is not derivation, and the identity above supplies only the former. The exponent was chosen as the closest of an enumerated candidate sweep which ranged well beyond the hook lengths, so a hook expression existing for the winner is a property of the hook lengths rather than evidence about the spectrum. Neither figure is a framework accuracy result. Two further facts bear on how far the identity can be carried: the k = 4 prediction was not testable as stated, the top eigenvalue there being degenerate; and \rho_k has k rows, so by the Schur–Weyl row cap every k \geq 3 names a block with no states at the framework's fibre dimension N = 2. The identity h_{\mathrm{corner}}(\rho_k) = 2k-1 is a theorem about the diagram and stands on its own.
